newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast gasoline prices weak, but rally seen.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast gasoline prices weak, but rally seen.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast gasoline fell Wednesday, as sellers lowered prices to keep pace with a lower energy futures market in New York.
But traders said the market would rebound soon, with a flotilla of imports factored into the market and the cost of raw crude falling relative to refined products.
"People are finally thinking its bottomed out," said one broker in California. "Cargoes are unlikely to come."
A 486,000 barrel cargo of gasoline reached Los Angeles April 3, a trader reported. Mobil and Chevron refineries bought the supply on the spot market, traders said.
Traders said four more cargoes have or would arrive soon, but could not give details.
Western spot prices, which attained a 20-cent premium over futures in recent weeks, have fallen to a nine cent advantage, leaving other regions without incentive to pay shipping costs west.
"Arbs are closed at this point," one trader said.

Supply and demand appeared balanced, with West Coast gasoline supplies up last week, but still 2.3 million barrels short of year-ago levels, American Petroleum Institute (API) said in its Tuesday stocks report.
And the region's huge refining output appeared to rebound after losing production during seasonal maintenance shutdowns.
West Coast refineries operated at 91 percent of capacity last week, up 1.2 percentage points from the previous week, API reported Tuesday.
Offers for CARB gasoline in Los Angeles were talked 70.50, 2.50 cents a gallon lower in Wednesday trade. San Francisco CARB gasoline was priced two cents lower by sellers at 69.50 cents.
CARB diesel fuel rose one cent in Los Angeles to 76/77 cents a gallon.
